researchQuestion: Which exact architectural instructions produce every observed 32-byte prepare_layer aggregate transition from the selected zero epoch through the exact-source marker when hardware watchpoint callback coalescing is removed?

prospectiveHypothesis.primary: Single-stepping the prospectively selected invocation with all software breakpoints disabled will expose a continuous bitwise aggregate state chain and assign each changed boundary to one exact instruction in a frozen QuartzCore scope.
prospectiveHypothesis.opaqueBoundary: Calls outside the seven frozen scopes will not change the selected aggregate across their entry-to-return boundary. Any changed opaque boundary is a null outcome and must open a separately preregistered successor scope.
prospectiveHypothesis.knownTransfer: The continuous state chain contains zero, [P,1024-P-640,640,640], [P,1024-P-640-8,640,648], and [floor(P)-1,1024-P-640-8,P+640-(floor(P)-1),P+648-(floor(P)-1)] bit-for-bit and in order.
prospectiveHypothesis.semanticSeal: Passing opens exact changed instruction bytes, operands, and before/after state only. Instruction semantics, the complete crop policy, unseen transfer, shader authority, and parity remain sealed.

selection.sourceSelection: Reuse the independent capture_backdrop late selector and its exact object chain.
selection.frameSelection: Accept exact prepare_layer function name and frozen symbol bounds only when the bounded live ancestry has exactly four exact prepare_layer frames and the top SBFrame.GetFP equals x29.
selection.futureIdentity: At +0x3ef0 require x28 to equal the independently selected source while threadID/x19/x29 still equal the stopped epoch identity.

instrumentation.unopenedScopeHashRule: The prior artifact fixed filterApply and filterMapBounds names, relative starts, and byte counts but not their complete bytes. Their runtime bytes and SHA-256 are captured before the first selected epoch resumes. Because every aligned instruction in each full symbol is stepped independent of content, the observed digest cannot influence instruction selection.
